issue.title: Enhancement: sonic-mgmt reboot tests could cause DUT to be stuck at grub edit mode

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the enhancement

More robust way to establish and clean up console connection in sonic-mgmt tests for reboots. Graceful handling of cleanup if console connection is not established - only write `exit` if at SONiC prompt.

### Current Behavior

sonic-mgmt reboot tests sometimes cause DUT to enter GRUB edit mode (as seen in console) when the reboot is happening. However, this is not expected or handled the test framework. So, the DUT is stuck, and the test fails / cannot proceed with remaining test cases. Typically, the DUT has to be recovered by power cycling.

As part of the `netmiko` framework, the cleanup of `SSHConsoleConn` can be triggered by many ways. In my limited experience, this is typically triggered by an EOF exception during a console read while the reboot is happening. When the cleanup sends `exit` ([ref](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/99b28c4f2072cead6ba6fff48821395eae75eda6/tests/common/connections/ssh_console_conn.py#L192)) as part of the clean up, it happens to coincide with the GRUB menu (which is normal during bootup). Sending `e` then enters the GRUB edit mode unexpectedly.

I think the cleanup is called correctly but should not blindly write `exit` to the console. In #24288 , the proposal is to first check that the console is likely at the SONiC prompt (which seems to be the original intent based on the comment there).

### Proposed Behavior

Console connection is established as best effort and should not be the cause of a test failure. Using it (or not) should not cause unrelated failure for reboot tests.

resolution.title: Improve console connection during sonic-mgmt reboot events
resolution.description:
### Description of PR

Summary: Improve establishing console connection in sonic-mgmt reboot test runs and avoid DUT console to be stuck at grub edit.
Fixes #24289

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [x] Test case improvement

### Back port request
- [ ] 202205
- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [x] 202511

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?

We have observed DUT is stuck in GRUB edit mode during sonic-mgmt tests that involve reboots.
The sonic-mgmt tests that use the `tests/common/reboot.py` helper attempts to create a console connection ([ref](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/99b28c4f2072cead6ba6fff48821395eae75eda6/tests/common/reboot.py#L390)) during which any exception (for example, EOF from console reads) could trigger a cleanup of the console connection. At the same time, the DUT has already started reboot. The cleanup writes exit ([ref](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/99b28c4f2072cead6ba6fff48821395eae75eda6/tests/common/connections/ssh_console_conn.py#L192)) to the console while the DUT gets to the grub menu. `e` typically enters the grub edit mode, which is not expected or handled by the test framework. So the DUT is stuck, and the test fails / cannot proceed with remaining test cases.

As part of the `netmiko`, the cleanup can be triggered by many ways. In my limited experience, this is typically triggered by an EOF exception during a console read while the reboot is happening. I think the cleanup is called correctly but should not blindly write `exit` to the console. The proposal is to first check that the console is likely at the SONiC prompt (which is the original intent based on the comment there).

As an aside, the PR also improves the way to establish console connection in the first place.

Example that causes a cleanup

```
   multiprocessing/pool.py worker
    └─ reboot.py:730  collect_console_log()
         └─ reboot.py:719  try_create_dut_console()
              └─ dut_utils.py:525  create_duthost_console()
                   └─ console_host.py:54  ConsoleHost()
                        └─ ssh_console_conn.py:52  SSHConsoleConn.__init__()
                             └─ base_console_conn.py:64  BaseConsoleConn.__init__()
                                  └─ netmiko/base_connection.py:495  __init__()
                                       └─ netmiko/base_connection.py:501  _open()
                                            └─ netmiko/base_connection.py:999  _try_session_preparation()
                                                 │  <————————————————————— Exception raised here (channel EOF or ReadTimeout)
                                                 └─ base_console_conn.py:112  disconnect()
                                                      └─ netmiko/base_connection.py:2488  disconnect()
                                                           └─ ssh_console_conn.py:218  cleanup()
                                                                └─ send_command("exit", expect_string="login:")

```

We observed at least 2 triggers for the exception
1. sonic-mgmt's [login_stage_2](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/f84006b6d63568478b4d97b953ad054f6551418d/tests/common/connections/ssh_console_conn.py#L61) -> "Socket is closed" ([ref](https://github.com/paramiko/paramiko/blob/8697158113a3eab25ed1d1d541ebe2cad10169a7/paramiko/channel.py#L1196)). Here, login failed because the device is rebooting.
2. sonic-mgmt [session_preparation](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/f84006b6d63568478b4d97b953ad054f6551418d/tests/common/connections/ssh_console_conn.py#L41) -> [ReadTimeout](https://github.com/ktbyers/netmiko/blob/develop/netmiko/base_connection.py#L812-L827) because it takes more than [20 seconds](https://github.com/ktbyers/netmiko/blob/eadebd7f59314708e11d8e5acd143957d9d74ebd/netmiko/base_connection.py#L1241) to go through BIOS and GRUB

The 20 second timeout became effective and surfaced the latent timing bug since https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/24306/ when the new `netmiko` version has a much shorter timeout.

#### How did you do it?

-  Instead of a hard coded sleep, block on establishing a console connection , with a time out (in which case console cleanup is not attempted anymore). Console connection is established as best effort and should not be the cause of a test failure.
- Attempt to clean up console connection only if at SONiC prompt. Before writing exit to console, make sure the console is already connected and is likely to be seeing the SONiC prompt.

#### How did you verify/test it?

Run these tests multiple times
- tests/platform_tests/test_kdump.py
- tests/platform_tests/test_power_off_reboot.py
- tests/platform_tests/test_reboot.py

Successful console connection is typically established after the first attempt
